connection_type: I have direct personal experience (as an immigrant, refugee, religious minority, or member of a marginalised group)
disclosure_text: I am a muslim south asian girl. I am a visible minority, and I have always stood out in crowds.
micronarrative: This happens to me. Whenever I want to share my culture or religious holidays, non people of colour act like I'm forcing my beliefs on them when that is not the case at all. I see it everyday on social media, where comments are islamophobic or racist. It happens to me in the sense that I ask to get time off from school or work so I can celebrate, and I get dirty looks. I do change how I phrase the request; I say that it's a personal thing that I want to celebrate with my family. This shift feels like both a protective measure and a source of distance. I want them to take me seriously and not think my culture or religion is a joke. The bakery probably just wanted to share their culture with people and people took it the wrong way.
